source_title: State of the Claw — OpenClaw Update
speaker: Peter Steinberger (Creator of OpenClaw, now at OpenAI)
key_insight: OpenClaw's 5-month track record proves multi-agent orchestrators face nation-state supply chain attacks, CVSS-slop noise, and unnerfed-model sandbox escapes — Lethal Trifecta mitigation and foundation governance are mandatory.

discovered_urls.context: Primary OpenClaw repo — cited stats (~30K commits, ~2K contributors, ~30K PRs, highest GH star count for non-educational OSS project)
Open Claw Foundation — to be launched; governance model inspired by Ghostty Foundation; bank setup almost complete; full-time maintainer hiring planned
Ghostty Foundation — the explicit template Peter copied for Open Claw Foundation structure; relevant blueprint for any OSS orchestrator transitioning to neutral governance
Simon Willison's Lethal Trifecta series — original framing Peter cites as the canonical agent-security threat model; directly applicable to our tmux worker permission matrix
OpenAI's Symphony orchestration layer — cited by Peter as evidence OpenAI supports open-source agent infra; Elixir-based process supervision for Codex fleets

'Agents of Chaos' paper — academic fearmongering example Peter criticizes; spent 4 pages explaining OpenClaw architecture, ignored published security docs, ran in 'pseudo mode' requiring code changes. Exact arxiv ID needs verification
Baseline comparison: Peter's 1,142 advisories / 16.6 per day claim vs Linux kernel ~8-9/day and curl ~600 lifetime. Worth validating these numbers for our own security-reporting heuristics
Axios NPM supply chain compromise — MS Teams and Slack pulled Axios unpinned, re-exposing OpenClaw indirectly. Reference case for transitive dependency hygiene in agentic frameworks
Full AIE Europe 2026 London session recording — Peter's talk starts ~timestamp t=5100s; other talks in same stream should be reviewed for additional ingestions
discovered_urls.suggested_ingest: Review for additional talks to ingest
